title: Restart test compares a route, not an address: a timed-out unix probe routes to the TCP understudy
body:
CI run 45328303838 (3.5.2 candidate at 029297dee) failed the_daemon_harness_can_restart::a_restart_replaces_the_process_and_keeps_the_address at tests/the_daemon_harness_can_restart.rs:50, on ubuntu-latest: left Some(Unix(<home>/.local/state/intent/run/intentd.sock)), right Some(Tcp(127.0.0.1:51737)), the same home.

`RealDaemon::endpoint()` is `daemon::route(candidates_under(home))`: the first candidate whose probe completes a round trip inside `PROBE_DEADLINE` (250ms). On a loaded runner the unix probe after the restart timed out, so the route fell to the TCP understudy, whose port is new with every daemon. The test compared a route, not the address its comment names ("derived from HOME alone"). The two arms are not a cross-test HOME race: the left is this test's own home.

mcp_bridge_restart.rs carried a tautological `endpoint() == endpoint()` assertion with the same exposure.

Fix (test-only): `RealDaemon::socket()` returns the socket path the home derives, and the restart test asserts that a plain `UnixStream::connect` to it succeeds after the restart (no probe deadline), so the new daemon is observed at the old address. The tautological assertion goes.


Resolution: fixed by f3a168417 on main, and shipped in tag v3.5.2 at fabbffd8c. Every leg of candidate run 45371863729 was green (local, macos and kovacs).
